account id (`https://api.openai.com/auth`.chatgpt_account_id), the
workspace the subscription bills. Another OAuth provider: the email its
credential names, if any, and its provider id. A key: its last four
characters (`…a1b2`) and, as `organization`, a fingerprint of it
(`key:` and the first 16 hex of its SHA-256), so the same key on two
machines is one account and the key itself never leaves them.

kind.description:
How the account signs in. Claude: a subscription (`claude auth login`) or a
Console organization (`claude auth login --console`). Any other provider:
its own OAuth sign-in through pi-ai (`oauth`), or a key (`api_key`).

HomeCredential.description: One credential in a harness's own store a CawCo account can hold.

provider.description: The account provider it is for.

storeProvider.description: The provider's id in that store, as the store names it (`openai` in OpenCode's for ChatGPT).

HomeStore.description: Where a credential moved into an account came from: a harness's own store on the machine.

UsageLimitsResponse.description:
What `/api/usage/limits` returns: every machine's latest readings. A
machine's Claude limits are those of the account it runs Claude Code on by
default (its `~/.claude` login), else of the first account signed in there.

ClaudeLimits.description:
A Claude account's limits, as its sessions' Claude Code reported them
(`rate_limit_event`, `accountInfo()`). A window whose `resetsAt` has passed
with no newer report reads 0%.

error.description: Why there are no windows: nothing on the account has reported any yet.

extraUsage.description: Extra usage as the last `rate_limit_event` said; null: it never said.

fetchedAt.description: When Claude Code last reported on the account.

stale.description:
No session runs on the account, so use from anywhere else goes unseen
and the windows are as of `fetchedAt`.

ClaudeExtraUsage.description: Extra usage: requests past the plan's limits, paid as they go.

inUse.description: Whether the account is spending extra usage now (`isUsingOverage`).

offReason.description:
Why it is off, in words from Claude Code's `overageDisabledReason`
("out of credits"); null when on or when it gave no reason worth saying.

on.description: Whether requests past the plan may run as extra usage (`overageStatus`).

resetsAt.description: When extra usage resets, when Claude Code said.

OpenCodeGoLimits.description:
The OpenCode Go plan's three windows, read from
`GET https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/usage` with the machine's `opencode-go`
key. Absent (null) on a machine with no Go key. `stale` is set when a read
failed and the last good windows are served with the error attached.

UsageSpend.description:
The fleet's real spend, as the hub reckons it and serves it at
`/api/usage/spend` and on every `kind: 'usage'` frame: the one figure every
"today" in CawCo reads.

Real money is opencode's own per-message cost; Claude is a subscription
whose constraint is a percentage, so its API-price estimate is never added
in. The days are the hub's: `todayStart` is local midnight and `weekStart`
this Monday's midnight in `timeZone`, the hub's own zone (IANA name).

UsageSummary.description: What `/api/usage/summary` returns: the groups, their totals, and unpriced models.

UsageSummaryRow.description:
One aggregated group in a usage summary. `key` is the group's identity (a
session id, a machine id, an hour's epoch ms); `label` is what a reader is
shown. Session rows carry their machine and the instance that ran them (null
for a session run outside CawCo); machine rows carry the machine.

UsageRowMachine.description: The machine a summary row ran on: named, never shown by id.

UsageTotals.description: The whole-window sums a summary's groups roll up to.

PlanSnapshot.description: Hub → a session's followers: the whole plan (AG-UI STATE_SNAPSHOT).

source.description:
Where the steps come from: CawCo's own list (`todo_write`'s session
scope), when the session's native to-do tools are denied ("CawCo's
to-dos" on, and always on pi, which has none); else the harness's own
list (Claude Code's task ledger, OpenCode's todos).

spec.description: The session's spec, once it has written one.

taskId.description: On a task attempt: the task.

todos.description: On a task attempt: the task's to-dos, nested and ticked as its file has them.

PlanDelta.description: Hub → a session's followers: the change from `rev - 1` to `rev` (AG-UI STATE_DELTA).

StreamBacklog.description:
Hub → client when the requested gap is inside its ring: events contiguous
ascending from `afterSeq + 1`. The client applies them in order, then
follows live deltas.

SessionStreamEvent.description:
One event on a session's canonical stream. `seq` is hub-assigned, monotonic
per session, starting at 1 — and NO GAP is ever delivered: a client that
observes `seq > lastSeq + 1` re-subscribes with `afterSeq = lastSeq` instead
of applying the delta.

sessionId.description: The instance id — what the dashboard calls a viewId.

SessionStreamFrame.description:
What a session's stream carries: the changes each frame made to its
transcript, as the hub built them (`transcript-types.ts`), and its preview's
state. Raw frames never reach a dashboard; the hub folds them.

SendRecord.description:
THE ONE RECORD OF A SEND. The hub writes it when it accepts the send and is
its only writer after that: every change is stored, then sequenced into the
session's stream as a `send` frame, and a history read serves it beside the
entries. Every screen draws the send from this, live and after any reload.

acceptedAt.description: ISO-8601: when the hub took the send. The only clock its row shows.

anchor.description:
A failed send the harness never stored: the uuid of the last thing the
session said before it failed — an assistant frame, or a send it read.
Its row goes right after that. Absent when the hub knew of nothing the
session had said: its row then goes after the last row dated before
`acceptedAt`, or first when none is.

body.description:
Exactly what the sender submitted: its words, its pictures (as the hub's
media references) and pastes, and who it is from. What the agent adds on
the way to the harness (a worktree line, an urgent prefix) is not in it.

harnessId.description:
The id the harness stored the send under, where that is not its uuid:
opencode's message id, pi's entry id, and — for a send Claude joined into
another's record ({@link SessionMessage.joined}) — that record's uuid.

reason.description: Why it failed, in the harness's words or the hub's.

replaces.description: The failed send this one was sent in place of.

NeutralUserMessage.description:
A user-role message. Two things wear this shape: what the harness says in
the user's role (tool results, its own notices), and a message SENT to the
session — which always carries `origin` and `uuid` ({@link SentMessage}),
and nothing else does.

compactSummary.description:
This message is a compaction's summary, in the harness's own words: pi
reports one when a compaction ends. Claude's needs no flag — it opens
with words the transcript knows it by.

replaces.description:
A retry: the uuid of the failed send this one is sent in place of. The
hub marks that record `replaced` ({@link SendRecord.replacedBy}).

timestamp.description: When the harness stored it ({@link NeutralAssistantMessage.timestamp}).

questionResult.description: The answer payload of an `AskUserQuestion` tool result, normalised by the harness adapter.

source.description:
The picture as the harness takes it (`base64`), or as the hub's
transcript and `send` records carry it: a reference into its media
store (`url`), fetched when the picture is shown.

SendMode.description:
How a send asks to be read: as a turn of its own, as a note the next turn
folds in (`shouldQuery: false`), or urgently — into the running turn, or
ahead of it.

SendState.description:
Where a send stands, as the hub alone decides it: waiting for the harness
(`pending`), taken up by it (`read`), never going to be (`failed`, with
why), or sent again as another send (`replaced`).

compactSummary.description:
This message is a compaction's summary, not an answer: opencode writes
its summary in the assistant's role (`summary: true` on the message).
Its text is the compaction's brief ({@link SessionMessage.compactSummary}).

contentOffset.description: Blocks already published for this message, preserving row ids across incremental settlement.

error.description:
The harness's word that this message is not the model answering but a
failure written in its place — Claude's synthetic `authentication_failed`,
`rate_limit`, … (measured on CLI 2.1.280: "Not logged in · Please run
/login" arrives as one, before an `is_error` result).

failedSends.description:
Set by the hub on an error message ({@link error}) that answered sends
the session had just read: they failed with its words, and their rows
carry them, so it draws no row of its own.

raw.description: The harness's own event, verbatim, for renderers that need more than this.

timestamp.description:
When the harness stored this record, ISO-8601: the clock its row shows,
live as after a reload ({@link SessionMessage.timestamp}). Claude's
stream carries its record's own; opencode's is its message's
`time.created`; pi's is its entry's. Absent on a frame the harness
stores no record for.

cache.description: Prompt-cache tokens the turn read from / wrote to, when the harness reports them.

cacheReusable.description: Claude's real turn began after every known prompt write had finished.

contextTokens.description:
pi and OpenCode: the tokens the turn's last request sent (uncached input
plus cache reads and writes, as the harness reports that request's
usage), which is the session's context as it stood. Claude's is read off
{@link promptCacheUsage}.

failedSends.description:
The sends this error failed, set by the hub: read, and answered by nothing
but this error. Their rows carry the error, so it draws no line of its own.

lastRequestAt.description: Agent receive time of the last main-loop requesting status, epoch ms.

recovered.description: Read from stored history during recovery, rather than a newly completed turn.

timestamp.description: When the harness stored what it closes on ({@link NeutralAssistantMessage.timestamp}).

turnUsage.description:
OpenCode and pi: the turn's tokens by model, summed over its assistant
messages and any compaction it ran. Claude's are read off the change in
its cumulative `modelUsage` by the hub.

NeutralSystemMessage.description:
A `system` frame. One loose interface rather than a subtype union: the folding
layer switches on `subtype` and reads the fields each subtype carries, and a
harness that emits a subtype nothing here names degrades to a generic line.

asked.description: Moved because a person asked (`POST /api/instances/:id/account`), not at a limit.

sameOrganization.description: Both accounts in one organization: its prompt cache came along.

window.description: The window that refused it, as {@link windowWords} names it.

resetsAt.description: When that window resets, epoch ms; null when nothing said.

because.description:
Why it moved before any limit refused it: its account was forecast
to run out at `runsOutAt` (a rebalance between turns), or its cache
was cold at its wake, so the move re-read nothing extra. Absent: its
account's limit refused a turn, or a person asked.

cost.description: What the re-read cost on `to`: a percent of its window; absent when unpriced.

until.description: The reset it waits for, epoch ms: the line counts down to it.

kind.description:
The session's summary is being written, on `to` (null: a harness
without accounts), for it to go on from in a fresh conversation:
the line it is until that conversation starts, when it becomes the
`continued` line under the same id, or `unmoved` if it failed.

asked.description: The session asked for it (`continue_session`), not its account's limit.

kind.description:
The session went on in a fresh conversation of its own, seeded with a
summary of the one before: the same session, its account changed
(`from` to `to`; null on a harness without accounts).

writtenOn.description: The account whose summariser wrote the summary it went on from.

asked.description: The session asked for it (`continue_session`), not its account's limit.

preparedAtPct.description: The window's percent when the summary was written ahead of the limit; null when it was written at the move.

kind.description:
A work item's session whose project has Caw off: nothing wakes a
model there, so nothing carries it on past `account`'s limit,
neither a move nor a resume at the reset. A person sends it on.

resetsAt.description: When that limit resets, epoch ms; null when nothing said.

kind.description: Continuing it on `to` failed at `step`: it goes on in its conversation, still on `from`.

asked.description: The session asked for it (`continue_session`), not its account's limit.

reason.description: What the hub got from the step that failed.

permissionMode.description:
How a session answers tool permissions. The union is Claude Code's, plus
`fullSend`, CawCo's own: Claude Code's `bypassPermissions` with the host
also answering the safety checks the CLI still raises in that mode. Each
adapter maps `fullSend` onto its harness; none hands it to an SDK as is.

result.description:
task_notification: the report a finished task handed back. Claude's live
frame carries none; its stored notification (`<result>`) does.

retry.description:
provider_retry ({@link PROVIDER_RETRY}): the provider's own message, and
when the harness makes its next attempt (ms epoch) if it said.

storedAs.description:
stored ({@link MESSAGES_STORED}), or read: the id the harness stores each
send under, by the send's uuid, where the harness keys its own record
differently (opencode's message id, pi's entry id). The hub keeps it on
the send's record, so a history read finds the send again.

whole.description:
held ({@link MESSAGES_HELD}): `held` is every send the harness has been
handed. Said by an agent taking over a process that outlived the one
before it, off the process's own output: a send from before then that is
not in it never reached the process.

ObservedRateLimitInfo.description:
The `rate_limit_info` payload, structurally. Not imported from the agent
SDK: `unifiedWindows` is marked `@internal` there, so it is stripped from
the published `.d.ts` even though the CLI emits it.

NeutralRawMessage.description: A frame that has no neutral meaning yet, forwarded whole for a future renderer.

kind.description: Hub-originated: a send's record, as it stands after its latest change.

StreamReset.description:
Hub → client when the gap is unrecoverable (older than the ring holds):
an honest refusal, never a partial replay. The client reads the newest
transcript page again and resumes from the `seq` it carries.

StreamDelta.description: Hub → client, live fan-out of one sequenced event.

PlanFollow.description:
Client → hub: the sessions whose plan this socket follows beside the ones
it streams (a thread showing its lead's plan), the whole set each time.
One newly in the set is answered with its snapshot; deltas follow.

PlanResync.description: Client → hub: "my copy has a gap; send the plan whole".

StreamSubscribe.description:
Client → hub. `afterSeq` present is a resume ("I have up to here — replay the
rest"): a client sends it with the `seq` its transcript page was read at, and
again after a reconnect. Absent is a fresh join ("start me from now").

CommandEnvelope.description:
Client → hub: an operator action as a durable, trackable object rather than
a fire-and-forget call. `commandId` is client-generated and unique per
submission; `payload` is exactly what the corresponding legacy relay
operation takes today.

CommandKind.description: The operations a command envelope can carry — 1:1 with existing relay ops.

kind.description: Daemon-originated: one send did not go; its record fails and the session goes on.

HeldSendFrame.description:
Daemon-originated: a send the machine was handed and no process took: it
found no live process for its session, or the process it was handed to went
away (slept, exited, failed, relaunched, refused by the session keeper)
before reading it. Whole, as it was sent, under the hand-off it was given
(`SendPayload.delivery`); the hub owes it to the session's next process.

TextAttachment.description:
What a turn carries beside its typed words, other than pictures: a text
the reader attached or pasted at length, folded into the prompt as quoted
material; or any other file, which the hub stores (`POST /api/files`) and
the session's machine fetches and puts on its own disk before the harness
sees the turn, naming its path in one line of the message.

ref.description: The hub's reference to its bytes: `/api/files/<sha256>`.

SentMessage.description:
A message sent to a session, by the reader or by cawco. `uuid` is its one
identity from the press to a reload: the dashboard's command id for a
reader's send, minted where the hub builds its own. The hub keeps one
{@link SendRecord} under it, and every copy of the message on every screen
is drawn from that record.

formerIds.description:
The ids sessions had before the hub folded each one's continuations at
its account's limit into it (migration 0128): former id → its id now. A
tab or link that names a former id is that session.

kind.description: Hub-originated: the complete board on every connection, including reconnects.

moves.description: Every project move the hub is carrying; each change after this arrives on the `moves` frame.

noticesSeen.description: The notice ids a person acknowledged, on any tab or device (hub notices.ts).

accountId.description:
The account the session runs on (`instances.account_id`): placed once as
it starts and kept for its whole life. Null on a harness without accounts
and on a session from before accounts existed.

autopilot.description:
The supervisor's standing autopilot for this session, set from the
composer popover. `null` means never configured; disabling keeps the
prompt rather than discarding it, so re-enabling does not mean retyping
it. Absent on a hub that predates the column.

canDelegate.description:
Whether the session may spawn delegates of its own — `false` on a leaf
delegate (spawned with `can_delegate: false`, the default). Null on a
session nobody delegated, which may.

cwd.description: The directory the session was launched in; see `launchDir`.

delegateType.description: The delegate type its spawn named; null: none.

delegateTypeProject.description: The project whose catalog that type came from; null: the fleet's.

derivedTitle.description:
The name the session's first user message gave it, derived once by the hub.
A listing already answers {@link title} with this when nothing named the
row, so a reader never watches the label change as the transcript arrives.

effort.description:
The effort the session actually sends, as its agent last read it back from
the harness ({@link import ("./harness").EFFORT_READ}): a level, `none` when
it sends no effort, null until the first reading lands. A restart hands a
level back to the new process, so it keeps working at the one it was on.

harness.description: Which harness owns {@link sessionId} — what a resume and a catalog read route on.

held.description: First-hand custody on the current agent connection, never stored liveness.

kind.description: `scratch` for a spin-off; absent from a hub that predates the column.

lastError.description: What killed the session, on a row the agent reported as `error`.

launchDir.description:
Whether `cwd` is the launch directory: `known`; `unread`, still to be read
from its machine; `unknown`, its machine has no record of its conversation,
so `cwd` may be a folder its CLI wandered into and the session is named by
its title (hub `sessionLabel`) and cannot be resumed.

parentInstanceId.description: The instance this one is a delegate of; absent for a mainline session.

parentToolUseId.description: The delegating tool call, so the parent transcript can render the round trip.

permissionMode.description:
How the session answers tool permissions and which model answers, as of its
last spawn, switch or `init`. Null on a session that has never said.

projectId.description: Set when the session was started from a project page.

role.description:
The toolset it runs in, when its spawn named one (a project's Caw is
`lead`); null: derived from how it started.

runningDelegates.description: Hub-derived count of live delegated work items, including descendants and checks.

seenAt.description:
When the owner last looked at it (its tab in front, after it ended) or
archived it off Finished, on any device. Null on one never seen.

sessionId.description: The harness's own session id, once the session has named itself.

threadId.description:
The thread with its project's Caw this session works for, when Caw's
work started it: the rail nests it under that thread.

title.description:
What the session is called: the owner's rename, else the name the session
gave itself (`set_title`) or was spawned under, else {@link derivedTitle}.

titleSource.description:
Who gave the session its name: `owner` (a dashboard rename, which the
session's own `set_title` cannot replace) or `agent`. Null while nobody has.

workItemId.description:
The work item this session runs: every delegate is one, and a session
never runs more than one. Null on a session nobody delegated, and on a
delegate from before work items existed.

InstanceStatus.description:
What a session row is doing, right now, as the hub last heard it.

- `starting` — a spawn went out and hasn't been confirmed live yet.
- `running` — the owning daemon currently lists the instance.
- `sleeping` — no live process, but it runs again: on the session id its
  harness picks back up from, or fresh under its id when it never named
  one ({@link relaunchOf}). This is what a daemon restart or a quiet drop used
  to report as `error` with {@link RESTART_RESUMABLE} in `lastError`; that
  encoding conflated "gone but fine" with a real failure, so `sleeping` rows
  carry `lastError: null` — nothing went wrong, there's just nothing running.
- `stopped` — deliberate: the operator (or a `stop` call) ended it.
- `error` — an actual failure. `lastError` is required here, and this is
  where {@link RESTART_LOST} still lands: a restart with nothing to resume
  from is a real loss, not a nap.
- `unknown` — the machine that owns this row can't currently be reached, so
  the hub can't say which of the above is true.
- `discarded` — a spin-off torn down on purpose; gone for good.
- `moving` — its project is moving to its machine for it (move.ts): the hub
  holds the row from the move's start, under the id the session starts
  under, and the move's start takes it on to `starting`. No process, and
  none is claimed: a failed move files it `error`, a cancelled one drops it.

agents.description: Changed machines only; omitted when no machine moved.

kind.description: Hub-originated: only changed rows and metadata; pulses travel separately.

presentation.description:
What the ask says on every surface, read once by the hub as it parks it
(permission-presentation.ts): the daemon's leg does not carry it, and the
hub fills it before anything else reads the frame.

processGeneration.description: The launch that raised this request; daemon replays retain it verbatim.

raisedAt.description: When the hub first parked this ask, ms epoch. Absent only on the daemon-to-hub leg.

requestKind.description: `tool` for a permission, `question` for an AskUserQuestion-shaped prompt.

threadId.description:
A project lead's question: the thread it was asked in (the one whose
message woke that turn, else the project's newest). Its answer lands in
that thread as your message.

toolUseId.description: The tool call the ask gates, as its transcript message names it.

asker.description: The session that asked, by the name the board gives it.

changes.description: The changes the call makes, each drawn as a diff. Empty when it changes no text.

detail.description: The line under the summary: how much changes and where ("3 lines changed in Working style").

fields.description: The rest of the input worth reading, secrets hidden. What the summary and the diffs already say is left out.

summary.description: What will happen and to what, in one line: "Change the fleet's CLAUDE.md".

PermissionChange.description: One file or document the call changes: both sides, for the diff renderers.

after.description: The text the proposed side ends with.

before.description: The text as it stands now ("" when there is none yet, or the call does not say).

path.description: What changes, named as the person knows it: `CLAUDE.md`, a memory path, a file path.

PermissionField.description: One input field, as shown: its value written out, secrets already hidden.

PermissionUpdate.description: A permission the SDK suggests persisting, so "always allow" has something to write.

kind.description: An ask is over, whoever settled it; every client removes its parked card.

reason.description:
Why a cancelled ask went unanswered, when the hub could say: it could not
show it at all (an ask from a session or launch it holds no live row for).
Such an ask was never parked on any screen, so this frame is the only
word a transcript gets of it.

toolName.description: The asking tool, for the line a screen writes about an ask it never held.

kind.description: Hub-originated: every machine's latest limits and the fleet's spend.

UsageLimitsReading.description:
One machine's latest limit reading, as the hub stores it (`usage_limits`)
and broadcasts it in a `kind: 'usage'` frame. `fetchedAt` is a `Date` inside
the hub and the ISO string it serialises to on the wire.

ended.description: Positive server-session receipt; absent receipts cannot confirm OpenCode.

kind.description: Authoritative daemon confirmation, never merely delivery of a stop request.

died.description:
Its process died on a signal while the daemon ran it, and nothing of the
daemon's stopped it (an OOM kill, a sessiond restart, a stray `kill`):
the signal, and the harness's own words. The hub starts it again with
the turn it cut, unless it died so right after the last such start.

kind.description: The daemon stopped an at-rest session's processes, or one ended of its own accord; its next message wakes it.
Recovery found no live handle; stored conversations remain resumable.
No `instanceId` when the call it answers was machine-scoped.

endReason.description: Internal end-reconciliation evidence; never relayed to a client.

kind.description: Hub-originated routing failures (e.g. target machine offline).

verb.description: The whole agent↔hub↔dashboard protocol. Adding a verb is a design decision.

ScratchWorktree.description: Creation provenance, stored by the agent and carried durably on its hub row.

attachments.description: Absolute paths of images on the session's machine to send alongside.

kind.description: Daemon-originated: a session pushing text straight to the owner's Telegram.
Daemon-originated: a session's coarse now-state, throttled to about once per second.

SessionPulse.description:
A coarse, now-state the rail draws without frames: what a session is doing
right now, folded on the daemon from the frames it is already pumping. It is
the *fallback* the dashboard reads for sessions it has not subscribed to —
open sessions still render the richer frame-fed state. `activity` is the same
three words the fleet view uses; `busy`/`runningSubagents` keep the finer
signals separate so a reader can still tell "blocked" from "working".

activity.description: Coarse now-state the rail draws without frames.

at.description: ms epoch of the last frame that changed this pulse.

currentTool.description: The tool the main loop is inside, addressed as the transcript addresses it.

kind.description: Hub-originated: a delegate work item's state; `instanceId` is its parent's.
Hub-originated: the session's standing offer, or null once it was answered.
Hub-originated: a thread was started, or its last message or status changed.
Hub-originated: a message was added to a thread.

Hub-originated: a project's tasks changed (one was created or moved, or
its folder was written), by anyone: read them again.

Hub-originated: the projects changed (one was made or forgotten, or a
place was added or removed: a checkout joined, a delegate's workspace
opened or was archived): read `/api/projects` again.

cap.description: Its project's cap as it stands now; null once it has none.

kind.description: Hub-originated: a project's spend against its cap moved, or the cap did.

ProjectStopFrame.description:
Hub-originated: one session a project's forget asked to stop
(`POST /api/projects/:id/stop`) has stopped, as its machine confirmed, or
could not be stopped, with the hub's reason, or (`deferred`) its machine is
away: its stop is recorded and is carried out when the machine registers
again. Never sent `stopped` for the request itself: a session is stopped
only once its machine says so.

error.description: Why it could not be stopped (`failed` only).

kind.description: Hub-originated: delegate traffic; `instanceId` is the delegate's.
Hub-originated: a supervisor verdict the moment it is logged.
Hub-originated, never stored: the supervisor began evaluating.

SupervisorStatusSignal.description:
Fired the moment an evaluation actually begins — the transient half of the
supervisor's visible life. Every evaluation is guaranteed to terminate in a
published {@link SupervisorEvent}, so a consumer can treat that event as
this signal's close; nothing here is persisted.

MovesFrame.description: Hub → dashboards and apps: every move job, whole, on each change.

MoveProgressFrame.description:
Daemon → hub: how far the step in flight is. `file` only while a file of
at least {@link LARGE_FILE_BYTES} is in flight (the largest).

WorkflowFrame.description: Hub-originated run transition, separate from a harness's session frames.

ask.description: Present while the run is `waiting`: everything needed to answer it.

checkpoint.description: The marker a `w.checkpoint` call just recorded.

seenAt.description: When the owner last looked at it or archived it, on any device.

seq.description: The effect sequence that owns this step: `ref` N in its run.

title.description:
What the call that opened the step named it: a `run`/`spawn` step's
title, an `ask`'s question, the workflow a `workflow` call started.
Null when the call named nothing.

IngestMark.description:
The hub's word on how far it has ingested one instance: the last line it
turned into a frame. Handed back on the register ack so a reattaching agent
replays exactly the gap the hub names — the mark is the hub's own, so the
agent's death loses nothing it needs.

WorkspaceRef.description: A workspace as the machine that holds it is told about it.

RepoInfo.description: One repository a machine can {@link SpawnPayload.bootstrap} from.

ToolState.description: What a probe or an install attempt found. The unit every surface renders.
